chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Nu'aym ibn Ibrahim from 'Abbad ibn Kathir al-Basri said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man freed his umm walad (concubine mother of his child) and made her manumission her dowry, then he divorced her before consummating the marriage with her. He said: He offers her that she be compensated for half of her value; if she refuses, then half of her is a slave and half is free.

key_terms.أُمّ وَلَدٍ: Concubine who bears her master's child

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an umm walad whose manumission was her dowry if she is divorced before consummation?
ai.summary: In this ruling from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial settlement for an umm walad whose manumission was structured as her dowry (sadaq) when divorced before consummation. The Imam offers her the choice to accept half her value as compensation for the remaining half of her freedom; if she refuses, she remains in a state of partial enslavement and partial freedom. This highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the valuation of freedom and the rights of the mother of a child in complex marital dissolution scenarios.
